blocks.text: People say a child 'has his father's nose'. Nothing physical was handed over — only a chemical message, coiled inside a single sperm cell too small to see. That message is DNA, and learning to read it is what genetics is.

blocks.markdown:
## From nucleus to gene

Inside the nucleus of every body cell are thread-like **chromosomes**, made of DNA wound around protein. Humans have 46 chromosomes — 23 pairs. The members of a pair are **homologous**: they carry genes for the same characteristics, in the same order, one inherited from each parent.

A **gene** is a length of DNA that codes for one protein and therefore controls one characteristic. Each gene occupies a fixed position, its **locus**, on a particular chromosome.

Most genes exist in alternative forms called **alleles**. The gene for seed shape in a pea, for example, has an allele for round and an allele for wrinkled. Because chromosomes come in pairs, every body cell carries two alleles of every gene — one on each homologous chromosome.

### The structure of DNA

A DNA molecule is a **double helix**: two long strands twisted around each other like a spiral staircase. Each strand is a chain of units called **nucleotides**, and each nucleotide is a sugar (deoxyribose) joined to a phosphate group and to one of four **bases**: adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G) and cytosine (C).

The two strands are held together by hydrogen bonds between the bases, and the pairing is strict:

- **A always pairs with T**
- **G always pairs with C**

This **complementary base pairing** is what makes accurate copying possible. When a cell prepares to divide, the two strands unzip and each acts as a template: wherever an A appears on the template a T is added to the new strand, and so on. The result is two identical double helices.

The **sequence of bases** along a gene is the genetic code. A group of three bases specifies one amino acid, so the base sequence determines the amino acid sequence of the protein, and the protein determines the characteristic.

blocks.caption: The vocabulary of genetics. Learn these before attempting any cross — most lost marks are vocabulary errors, not reasoning errors.

blocks.title: Genotype and phenotype
blocks.text: The genotype is the genetic instruction; the phenotype is the visible result. Two organisms can share a phenotype but differ in genotype: a TT pea and a Tt pea are both tall, yet only the Tt one can produce a dwarf offspring.

blocks.title: Keeping the chromosome number constant
blocks.prompt: A maize plant has 20 chromosomes in each of its root cells. State the number of chromosomes in its pollen grain nucleus and in the zygote formed after fertilisation, and explain how the number stays constant across generations.

steps.text: A root cell is a body cell, so 20 is the diploid number: 2n = 20, meaning 10 homologous pairs.
Pollen contains the male gamete, which is formed by meiosis. Meiosis separates the members of every pair, so the gamete is haploid: n = 10.
The egg cell in the ovule is formed by meiosis too, so it also carries 10 chromosomes.
At fertilisation the two haploid nuclei fuse: 10 + 10 = 20. The zygote is therefore diploid again, with 20 chromosomes.

The zygote then grows entirely by mitosis, which copies chromosomes exactly, so every body cell of the new plant also has 20. The halving by meiosis and the doubling by fertilisation cancel out exactly, which is why the number is the same in every generation.

blocks.answer: Pollen grain nucleus: 10 chromosomes. Zygote: 20 chromosomes. Meiosis halves the number when gametes form and fertilisation restores it, so the diploid number is maintained generation after generation.

blocks.markdown:
### Mutation

A **mutation** is a sudden change in the genetic material. A **gene mutation** alters the base sequence of a single gene — sickle cell anaemia results from one base change in the haemoglobin gene. A **chromosomal mutation** alters the number or structure of chromosomes — Down syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome 21.

Most mutations are harmful or neutral, but a rare favourable one is the ultimate source of all new alleles, and therefore of the variation on which evolution depends. Mutation rates are raised by **mutagens**: ionising radiation such as X-rays and gamma rays, ultraviolet light, and chemicals including those in tobacco smoke.

blocks.title: Write alleles carefully
blocks.text: Use the same letter for both alleles of a gene, capital for dominant and lower case for recessive: T and t, never T and d. Using two different letters implies two different genes and loses marks in every cross you attempt.

points: Chromosomes are made of DNA and occur in homologous pairs in body cells; humans have 23 pairs.
A gene is a length of DNA coding for one characteristic, and alleles are its alternative forms.
DNA is a double helix in which adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine, which allows exact copying.
Genotype is the alleles present, phenotype is the observable result; homozygous means the two alleles are the same and heterozygous that they differ.
Meiosis halves and fertilisation restores the chromosome number, and mutation is the original source of new alleles.
